label: Filter Bar
title: Filter Bar
summary: Use a Filter Bar at the top of a list so people can narrow what they see by typing.
corePrinciple: Name what is being searched, then let the list below respond to every keystroke.

anatomy.title: A padded search field
anatomy.description: The bar holds one public Text Input set up for search, inset from the screen edges.
blocks: Full-width container that insets the field from the screen edges.
Fully rounded input surface from the public Text Input.
Names what is being searched until they type.

configuration.title: Only the words change
configuration.description: The bar, field, and icon come from tokens. Designers choose the placeholder and whether the bar opens with a query already in place.
blocks: The generic word says nothing about what can be found.
Naming the list tells people what they can find.
Use it when returning to a list that is already filtered.

states.title: Empty, filled, and focused
states.description: Filter Bar has no disabled or error state. It shows its placeholder when empty, the query when filled, and an outline while focused.
blocks: Select the field: a 1 px ring outlines its padded area without changing the bar’s height.

examples.title: Focused
examples.description: Select the field: a 1 px ring outlines its padded area without changing the bar’s height.

sizing.title: It always fills its host
sizing.description: Filter Bar takes the full width of its container and keeps a fixed height. Place it in a full-width row; the screen owns the width.
blocks: The field shrinks with its host while the bar keeps its padding.

examples.title: 240 px column
examples.description: The field shrinks with its host while the bar keeps its padding.

content.title: Say what can be found
content.description: Start with “Search” and name the list. Keep it to three words or fewer so it fits a narrow field.

inContext.title: Filter a transaction list
inContext.description: The screen passes the query to its list and shows only matching rows. Filter Bar reports the text; it does not filter anything itself.

doDont.title: Make search predictable
doDont.description: Each pair shows what people see when the placeholder or placement changes.
blocks: “Search transactions” tells people what they will find.
“Type here” hides what the field searches.
The whole placeholder stays readable in a narrow field.
A long prompt is cut off, so people lose what it searches.
One field, one set of results.
Two bars make people guess which one filters the list.

sources.title: Use the public Filter Bar contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Declared and installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 from the team’s private package repository. Figma draws the bar at 360 × 64 with a 44 px field; the installed package renders 62 px with a 42 px field. The focus outline is a fixed 1 px dark ring (not a token) that keeps the bar’s height. On the web, accessibilityLabel names the input. renderInput and children are developer overrides and are not shown.
